title: B2 · L23 — Phrasal verbs: money
topic: Phrasal verbs for finances and spending
description: Phrasal verbs financieros: pay off, splash out, save up, dip into, put aside, run up.

questions.prompt: Un amigo celebra haber terminado su hipoteca.
questions.question: What does 'to pay off a debt' mean?
options: To completely pay all the money owed.
questions.explanation: 'Pay off' significa liquidar por completo una deuda. Es específico para deudas: hipotecas, préstamos, tarjetas de crédito, préstamos estudiantiles. 'Pay off' también tiene un segundo significado ('resultar rentable': 'the investment paid off'), que el contexto aclara.
examples: It took her nearly ten years to pay off her mortgage — huge milestone. → hito vital
I finally paid off my student loan last week. Feels like a weight off my shoulders.

questions.prompt: Una amiga se regala un capricho de cumpleaños.
questions.question: Complete: 'She ___ ___ on a new designer handbag for her birthday.'
questions.explanation: 'Splash out (on)' significa gastar mucho dinero en algo especial o extravagante — con matiz de gasto PLACENTERO, no necesario. La preposición fija es 'on' + objeto. Es muy usado para bodas, vacaciones, regalos caros. Suena celebratorio; en cambio, 'shell out' o 'fork out' sugieren gasto forzado.
examples: We splashed out on a proper five-star hotel for our anniversary. Worth every penny. → celebración especial
He splashed out on a sports car for his 50th — classic midlife crisis energy.

questions.statement: 'To save up for something' significa juntar dinero gradualmente para un propósito específico.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Save up for' implica ahorrar con un OBJETIVO CONCRETO en mente (viaje, coche, casa, boda). Es distinto de 'save' general (ahorrar sin más). La preposición fija es 'for' + objetivo. Muy útil en conversaciones sobre planes vitales o metas financieras.
examples: I've been saving up for a trip to Japan for the past two years. → objetivo vital
They saved up for over a decade to finally buy their first house in a decent area.

questions.text: We had to dip into our savings to cover the unexpected medical bills last month.
questions.explanation: 'Dip into (savings)' significa echar mano puntualmente de los ahorros. La imagen es la de meter la mano en el bote. Sugiere uso NO PLANEADO y a menudo con leve incomodidad. Prosodia: pausa suave tras 'savings', énfasis en 'unexpected'. Connected speech: 'dip into' se pronuncia fluidamente 'dɪp-ɪntə'.
examples: I had to dip into my emergency savings to pay for the boiler repairs. → imprevisto doméstico
Try not to dip into your emergency fund unless it's a genuine emergency. → consejo financiero

questions.prompt: Un amigo se ha pasado con la tarjeta de crédito.
questions.question: What does 'to run up a bill' mean?
options: To accumulate a large bill or debt.
To refuse to pay a bill.
questions.explanation: 'Run up' (a bill/debt/tab) significa acumular una deuda considerable, a menudo poco a poco. Común con tarjetas de crédito, cuentas de bar/restaurante ('run up a tab') o gastos hospitalarios. Tono negativo — implica falta de control financiero. Metáfora: subir corriendo la escalera de la deuda.
examples: He ran up a huge bill on his credit card and now can barely make minimum payments.
They ran up debts they simply couldn't repay. Ended up filing for bankruptcy. → historia trágica

questions.statement: 'To put money aside' significa reservarlo para usarlo después.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Put aside' (o 'set aside') significa apartar, reservar dinero para un uso futuro. Es sinónimo de planificación financiera responsable. Muy usado en consejos de finanzas personales: 'put aside for retirement', 'put aside for emergencies'. Tono positivo, prudente, adulto.
examples: I put aside £200 every single month for our future house deposit. → disciplina financiera
It's genuinely wise to put some money aside for emergencies — you never know when.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada verbo financiero con su continuación natural:
questions.explanation: Cada phrasal tiene su matiz específico: pay off (liquidar deuda), splash out (gastar en lujo), save up (juntar para objetivo), dip into (usar ahorros puntualmente), put aside (reservar sistemáticamente). Todos son fundamentales para hablar de gestión personal del dinero.
examples: I splashed out on a really nice dinner for our anniversary. No regrets. → celebración
We're saving up for a big trip to South America next year. → planificación viajera

questions.prompt: Un mecánico te acaba de pasar un presupuesto altísimo.
questions.question: What does 'to shell out' mean?
options: To pay a large amount of money, often reluctantly.
questions.explanation: 'Shell out' significa desembolsar (a regañadientes) una cantidad considerable. Similar a 'fork out'. Enfatiza que el gasto es alto y NO deseado — opuesto tonal a 'splash out'. Muy usado en quejas cotidianas: 'I had to shell out for...', 'we ended up shelling out...'.
examples: I had to shell out £500 for car repairs this morning. Brutal. → queja mecánica
We shelled out an absolute fortune on our wedding — worth it, but ouch.

questions.target: I've been saving up for years to buy my first flat, but property prices keep going up faster than I can save.
questions.explanation: Reflexión típica del inquilino millennial/Gen-Z en cualquier gran ciudad. 'Property prices go up' es colocación estándar. Prosodia: tono ligeramente frustrado, énfasis en 'faster than I can save'. Nativos añaden 'honestly', 'at this rate', 'it feels impossible' para reforzar la queja generacional.
examples: I've been saving up for years for a proper trip around Southeast Asia. Finally happening in October.
Prices keep going up, but salaries somehow don't. It's genuinely getting harder to save. → charla generacional

questions.prompt: Un asesor financiero da un consejo básico a un joven.
questions.question: Complete: 'Try to ___ ___ money for retirement while you're young.'
questions.explanation: 'Put aside money for retirement' es un consejo financiero clásico. La preposición 'for' señala el propósito. 'Run up' sería catastrófico (acumular deuda), 'pay off' presupone deuda existente, y 'dip into' es usar ahorros existentes. Sólo 'put aside' encaja como acción constructiva a futuro.
examples: Put aside a little each week, even if it's just £20. It adds up faster than you think.
It's never too early to put money aside — compound interest is your best friend.

questions.statement: 'To cut back on spending' significa gastar más dinero.
questions.explanation: FALSO — significa lo CONTRARIO. 'Cut back on' significa reducir el consumo, gasto o cantidad de algo. Muy usado con gastos, calorías, alcohol, tiempo de pantalla. Sinónimo casi intercambiable: 'cut down on'. Ambos son fundamentales para hablar de moderación o ajuste presupuestario.
examples: We really need to cut back on eating out — it's killing our budget. → decisión financiera
The company cut back on marketing costs by 20% after a rough quarter.

questions.text: After losing his job, he had to cut back on non-essential expenses like dining out and holidays.
questions.explanation: Situación real de ajuste económico tras despido. 'Cut back on + sustantivo/-ing' es la estructura correcta con preposición fija 'on'. Prosodia: tono práctico, sin drama. Connected speech: 'cut back on' se enlaza como 'kʌt-bæk-ɒn'. 'Non-essential expenses' es vocabulario B2+ útil en contextos de presupuesto.
examples: We cut back on our travel spending significantly this year to save for the wedding.
You should probably cut back on sugar — your doctor's been mentioning it for years.

questions.prompt: Un CFO habla de la estrategia trimestral en una call de resultados.
questions.question: Complete: 'The company is looking to ___ ___ costs by ten percent this quarter.'
questions.explanation: 'Bring down costs/prices' significa reducir en registro empresarial. Muy común en contextos corporativos y análisis financiero. Sinónimos: 'reduce', 'lower', 'cut', 'trim'. 'Run up' sería el opuesto (acumular deuda), y 'splash out' es gasto placentero — ambos incorrectos aquí.
examples: They brought down prices aggressively to attract new customers. → estrategia comercial
We need to bring down our operating costs before the next board review.

questions.target: I splashed out on a really nice camera last month, but now I'm regretting it because I need to pay off my credit card.
questions.explanation: Combina 'splash out' (gasto placentero) con 'pay off' (liquidar deuda). Historia universalmente relatable de arrepentimiento post-compra impulsiva. Prosodia: entusiasmo inicial en 'really nice camera' que se convierte en resignación en 'regretting it'. Nativos añaden 'you know how it is' o 'shouldn't have done it, honestly'.
examples: I splashed out on a designer bag last month. My future self is going to hate me for it.
I really need to pay off my credit card debt before it snowballs. → autoconciencia financiera

questions.prompt: Un amigo declina una salida cara.
questions.question: What does 'to be strapped for cash' mean?
options: To have a lot of money.
To have very little money available.
questions.explanation: 'Strapped for cash' es una expresión idiomática coloquial para decir 'corto de dinero, sin liquidez'. Sinónimos: 'skint' (muy UK), 'broke' (universal), 'short on cash'. Es fórmula típica para declinar planes caros sin sonar dramático. Nota: es informal — no la uses en registro corporativo o formal.
examples: I'm a bit strapped for cash this month — can we do something cheaper? → propuesta alternativa
Sorry, I can't help you out this time — I'm properly strapped for cash myself.
